evals.prompt: I'm building a Next.js app with Fabricator UI (base-nova style, lucide icons). Create a settings form component with fields for: full name, email address, and notification preferences (email, SMS, push notifications as toggle options). Add validation states for required fields.
evals.expected_output: A React component using FieldGroup, Field, Switch, data-invalid/aria-invalid validation, gap-* spacing, and semantic colors.
expectations: Uses FieldGroup and Field components for form layout instead of raw div with space-y
Uses Switch for independent on/off notification toggles (not looping Button with manual active state)
Uses data-invalid on Field and aria-invalid on the input control for validation states
Uses gap-* (e.g. gap-4, gap-6) instead of space-y-* or space-x-* for spacing
Uses semantic color tokens (e.g. bg-background, text-muted-foreground, text-destructive) instead of raw colors like bg-red-500
No manual dark: color overrides

evals.prompt: Create a dialog component for editing a user profile. It should have the user's avatar (https://github.com/gabrielespinheira.png, @gabrielespinheira) at the top, input fields for name and bio, and Save/Cancel buttons with appropriate icons. Using Fabricator UI with the radix-nova style and tabler icons.
evals.expected_output: A React component with DialogTitle, Avatar+AvatarFallback, data-icon on icon buttons, no icon sizing classes, tabler icon imports, asChild triggers.
expectations: Includes DialogTitle for accessibility (visible or with sr-only class)
Avatar component includes AvatarFallback
Icons on buttons use the data-icon attribute (data-icon="inline-start" or data-icon="inline-end")
No sizing classes on icons inside components (no size-4, w-4, h-4, etc.)
Uses tabler icons (@tabler/icons-react) instead of lucide-react
Uses asChild for custom triggers (radix base)

evals.prompt: Create a dashboard component that shows 4 stat cards in a grid. Each card has a title, large number, percentage change badge, and a loading skeleton state. Using Fabricator UI with the base-nova style and lucide icons.
evals.expected_output: A React component with full Card composition, Skeleton for loading, Badge for changes, semantic colors, gap-* spacing.
expectations: Uses full Card composition with CardHeader, CardTitle, CardContent (not dumping everything into CardContent)
Uses Skeleton component for loading placeholders instead of custom animate-pulse divs
Uses Badge component for percentage change instead of custom styled spans
Uses semantic color tokens instead of raw color values like bg-green-500 or text-red-600
Uses gap-* instead of space-y-* or space-x-* for spacing
Uses size-* when width and height are equal instead of separate w-* h-*

evals.prompt: I'm building a Next.js app with Fabricator UI (base-nova style, lucide icons). Build a chat conversation view: a scrollable thread of messages from two different people, each with an avatar, sender name, timestamp, and message bubble. A couple of messages include an image attachment and a PDF file attachment, and there's a 'Today' divider separating the days.
evals.expected_output: A React component composing MessageScroller, Message, Bubble, Attachment, and Marker from the @fabricator registry instead of hand-rolled bubble/divider/attachment markup.
expectations: Uses MessageScroller (MessageScrollerProvider, MessageScrollerViewport, MessageScrollerContent, MessageScrollerItem) for the scrollable thread instead of a raw overflow-y-auto div or ScrollArea
Wraps each row in MessageScrollerItem inside MessageScrollerContent
Uses Message with MessageAvatar/MessageContent/MessageHeader for row layout instead of custom flex divs
Uses Bubble + BubbleContent for the message surface instead of a styled div with bg-muted/bg-primary
Uses Attachment (AttachmentMedia, AttachmentContent, AttachmentTitle, AttachmentDescription) for the file and image attachments instead of Item or a custom card
Uses Marker (variant="separator") for the 'Today' divider instead of Separator plus a centered label
Uses semantic color tokens and gap-* spacing; no raw colors like bg-emerald-500 and no space-y-*
Includes "use client" when the component uses state or event handlers (project.rsc)

evals.prompt: Using Fabricator UI (base-nova style, lucide icons), build a streaming AI chat UI. The assistant's reply streams in while it generates, the view auto-scrolls to follow the latest content but stops following if the user scrolls up to read earlier messages, a 'jump to latest' button appears when the user has scrolled away from the bottom, and a subtle 'thinking…' shimmer shows while the model is generating.
evals.expected_output: A React component that delegates scroll/anchor behavior to MessageScroller and uses MessageScrollerButton for jump-to-latest and the shimmer utility for the thinking indicator — no hand-rolled scroll logic or custom shimmer keyframes.
expectations: Uses MessageScroller with MessageScrollerProvider (autoScroll) and scrollAnchor on message items for the stick-to-bottom/follow behavior instead of a custom useStickToBottom hook or ResizeObserver/scrollTop wiring
Uses MessageScrollerButton for the jump-to-latest control instead of a hand-built conditional button driven by manual scroll-position state
Uses the shimmer utility class for the 'thinking…' indicator instead of a custom @keyframes or bg-clip-text gradient animation
Wraps each message row in MessageScrollerItem inside MessageScrollerContent
Uses Message + Bubble + BubbleContent for the conversation rows instead of hand-rolled bubble divs
Uses semantic color tokens and gap-* spacing; includes "use client" (project.rsc)

evals.prompt: Add a button, a dialog and a date picker to my existing Vite project. It already has a components.json with "style": "radix-vega" but no @fabricator registry. I want to keep my current look.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Fabricator CLI to add the @fabricator registry in blend mode and install components by bare name, without changing the style id.
expectations: Runs the Fabricator CLI (npx/pnpm dlx/yarn dlx/bunx fabricator-ui@latest), not a hand-written fetch of component files
Keeps the current look via blend mode: `fabricator-ui init --yes` / the 'add @fabricator registry only' option, or `--blend`
Installs with bare names (e.g. `fabricator-ui add button dialog`), which resolve to @fabricator, or explicit @fabricator/<name> addresses
Does not change the `style` field to a custom value such as "fabricator"; it stays "radix-vega"
Checks the installed components list or uses `search`/`docs` before writing code that imports the new components
Uses asChild for the dialog trigger (radix base)

evals.prompt: My project uses Fabricator UI with the aria base (aria-nova). Add a settings dropdown menu and a confirm-delete dialog to the header.
evals.expected_output: React Aria composition: triggers wrap the Button and the overlay, onPress handlers, no asChild/render, DialogTitle present, docs fetched first.
expectations: Runs `fabricator-ui docs <component>` (or fetches the docs URLs) before writing aria code
Uses DropdownMenuTrigger / DialogTrigger (or AlertDialogTrigger) wrapping a Button and the overlay, not asChild or render props
Uses onPress on Button rather than onClick
Includes a dialog title (DialogTitle or AlertDialogTitle) for accessibility
Groups menu items inside DropdownMenuGroup
Uses Sonner (toast from sonner) if it shows a toast after deleting

evals.prompt: Switch my Fabricator UI project to preset code a2r6bw. I've customized button.tsx and card.tsx and don't want to lose those edits.
evals.expected_output: Asks or chooses the merge path: init --preset --force --no-reinstall, then per-component dry-run/diff merges; never overwrites without approval.
expectations: Does not decode the preset code manually or build an init URL by hand
Uses `fabricator-ui init --preset a2r6bw --force --no-reinstall` (merge) or `fabricator-ui apply a2r6bw --only theme,font` rather than a plain `apply` that would reinstall components
Uses `fabricator-ui add <component> --dry-run` and `--diff <file>` (or `fabricator-ui diff <component>`) to merge customized components individually
Does not pass --overwrite without the user's explicit approval
Runs commands inside the user's project directory
